Indigenous Health Assessment (Adults 15–54 years)

Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • Painful, itchy, dry, cracked skin on palms for 3–4 months, worsening, interfering with work; likely contact dermatitis from cleaning products.  
  • Type 2 diabetes mellitus.  
  • Occupational exposure: hotel housekeeping, often cleans without gloves.
- Relevant family medical history:
  • Diabetes (type not specified).  
  • No known family skin disease, asthma, or bowel disorders.
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  • Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • E45 emollient cream (OTC) – no benefit.  
  • OTC antihistamine – name/dose/frequency not documented.  
  • New prescription to be issued: topical steroid cream (strength/dose not specified) and stronger emollient – instructions to apply 3–4 times daily.
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.
- Sexual and reproductive health: Not recorded.
- Physical activity and nutrition: Not recorded.
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:
  • Alcohol: “a couple of pints a week.”  
  • Tobacco: Non-smoker.  
  • Other substances: Not recorded.
- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): Not recorded; patient reports feeling generally well.
- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded.
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities: Works as a hotel housekeeper; no other social details recorded.

- BP, pulse rate and rhythm: Not recorded.
- Height, weight, BMI, waist circumference (if indicated): Not recorded.

- Ear exam (otoscopy, whisper test if needed): Not recorded.

- Fasting BGL and lipids (or random BGL if needed): Not recorded.
- Cervical screening (if eligible and due): Not recorded.
- STI screen (urine or swab – chlamydia/gonorrhoea if age 15–35): Not applicable (age 45); not recorded.
- Mammogram (if eligible): Not recorded.
- Other pathology (e.g., HbA1c, iron studies, Vitamin D): Not recorded.

Management Plan

- Assessment: Likely occupational contact dermatitis of palms; type 2 diabetes noted.
- Treatment:
  • Prescription for topical steroid cream plus stronger emollient; apply generously 3–4 times daily for 10–14 days.  
  • Advise strict avoidance of irritants; wear protective gloves for all cleaning tasks.
- Follow-up:
  • Review in 1–2 weeks; return sooner if symptoms worsen, spread, or fail to improve.  
  • Consider alternative therapies or dermatology referral if no response.
- Patient education provided on trigger avoidance and correct cream application.
- Work advice: Currently off work 3 days; encouraged to resume with glove use once symptoms allow.

● Internal contradictions: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; limited physical exam and preventive health information due to telehealth context.
